study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative modelling to detect disease progression in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease in a cross-sectional multi-cohort study

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Train a deep autoencoder-based normative model on UK Biobank healthy controls and quantify individual deviations in MCI/AD across multiple cohorts; compare deviation-based discrimination to traditional classifiers.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly states that UK Biobank data was used to train the normative models. The study used 11,034 healthy controls from UK Biobank who had data collected from the same MRI scanner (Cheadle centre) and were aged between 47 and 73 years old.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Here, we used an early release of the project's data comprising of 11,034 HC participants. The inclusion criteria for the present study were: (a) subjects who had the data collected in the same MRI scanner (from Cheadle centre), (b) age between 47 ND 73 years old.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Deviation scores increased with disease severity (HC < EMCI < LMCI < AD); deviations localized to medial temporal and ventricular regions; normative model showed comparable cross-cohort generalizability to traditional classifiers.
